questions.q: What did Moses anoint and sanctify for Yahweh on the day that the tabernacle and altar were completed?
questions.a: He anointed and sanctified the tabernacle, all its furnishings, the altar and all it’s utensils for Yahweh.

questions.q: What did the leaders of Israel bring as sacrifices in front of the tabernacle?
questions.a: They brought six covered carts and twelve oxen as sacrifices in front of the tabernacle.

questions.q: To whom did Moses give the offerings?
questions.a: Moses gave the offerings to the Levites, to each one as his work needed them.

questions.q: What did Gershon and his descendants receive because of what their work needed?
questions.a: Gershon and his descendants received two carts and four oxen.

questions.q: What did Merari and his descendants receive because of what their work needed?
questions.a: Merari and his descendants received four carts and eight oxen.

questions.q: Why did not the descendants of Kohath receive any of the carts and oxen given as offerings?
questions.a: The descendants of Kohath did not receive any of the carts and oxen given as offering because they carried the equipment and objects reserved for the tabernacle on their shoulders.

questions.q: When was each leader to offer their goods for the dedication of the altar?
questions.a: On their own day each leader offered their sacrifices in front of the altar.

questions.q: Who was the first of the 12 tribes of Israel that offered sacrifices for the dedication of the altar?
questions.a: Judah was the first of the 12 tribes of Israel that offered sacrifices for the dedication of the altar.

questions.q: On the 2nd day, which of the 12 tribes of Israel offered sacrifices for the dedication of the altar?
questions.a: On the 2nd day, Issachar of the 12 tribes of Israel offered sacrifices for the dedication of the altar.

questions.q: On the 3rd day, which of the 12 tribes of Israel offered sacrifices for the dedication of the altar?
questions.a: On the 3rd day, Zebulun of the 12 tribes of Israel offered sacrifices for the dedication of the altar.

questions.q: On the 4th day, which of the 12 tribes of Israel offered sacrifices for the dedication of the altar?
questions.a: On the 4th day, Reuben of the 12 tribes of Israel offered sacrifices for the dedication of the altar.

questions.q: On the 5th day, which of the 12 tribes of Israel offered sacrifices for the dedication of the altar?
questions.a: On the 5th day, Simeon of the 12 tribes of Israel offered sacrifices for the dedication of the altar.

questions.q: On the 6th day, which of the 12 tribes of Israel offered sacrifices for the dedication of the altar?
questions.a: On the 6th day, Gad of the 12 tribes of Israel offered sacrifices for the dedication of the altar.

questions.q: On the 8th day, which of the 12 tribes of Israel offered sacrifices for the dedication of the altar?
questions.a: On the 8th day, Manasseh of the 12 tribes of Israel offered sacrifices for the dedication of the altar.

questions.q: On the 9th day, which of the 12 tribes of Israel offered sacrifices for the dedication of the altar?
questions.a: On the 9th day, Benjamin of the 12 tribes of Israel offered sacrifices for the dedication of the altar.

questions.q: On the 11th day, which of the 12 tribes of Israel offered sacrifices for the dedication of the altar?
questions.a: On the 11th day, Asher of the 12 tribes of Israel offered sacrifices for the dedication of the altar.

questions.q: On the 12th day, which of the 12 tribes of Israel offered sacrifices for the dedication of the altar?
questions.a: On the 12th day, Naphtali of the 12 tribes of Israel offered sacrifices for the dedication of the altar.

questions.q: On the 10th day, which of the 12 tribes of Israel offered sacrifices for the dedication of the altar?
questions.a: On the 10th day, Dan of the 12 tribes of Israel offered sacrifices for the dedication of the altar.

questions.q: From what place did Yahweh speak to Moses when he was in the tent of meeting?
questions.a: Yahweh spoke to Moses from above the atonement lid on the ark of the covenant decrees, between the two cherubims.

commentary.text: The offerings of the princes at the dedication of the tabernacle.
The offerings of the princes at the dedication of the altar.

Verses 1–9 The offering of the princes to the service of the tabernacle was not made till it was fully set up. Necessary observances must always take place of free-will offerings. The more any are advanced, the greater opportunity they have of serving God and their generation. No sooner was the tabernacle set up, than provision is made for the removal of it. Even when but just settled in the world, we must be preparing for changes and removes, especially for the great change.

The princes and great men were most forward in the service of God. Here is an example to those in authority, and of the highest rank; they ought to use their honour and power, their estate and interest, to promote religion and the service of God in the places where they live. Though it was a time of joy and rejoicing, yet still, in the midst of their sacrifices, we find a sin-offering. As, in our best services, we are conscious that there is sin, there should be repentance, even in our most joyful services. In all approaches to God we must by faith look to Christ as the Sin-offering. They brought their offerings each on a day. God's work should not be done confusedly, or in a hurry; take time, and we shall have done the sooner, or, at least, we shall have done the better. If services are to be done for twelve days together, we must not call it a task and a burden. All their offerings were the same; all the tribes of Israel had an equal share in the altar, and an equal interest in the sacrifices offered upon it. He who now spake to Moses, as the Shechinah or Divine Majesty, from between the Cherubim, was the Eternal Word, the second Person in the Trinity; for all God's communion with man is by his Son, by whom he made the world, and rules the church, who is the same yesterday, to-day, and for ever.
